#| label: setup

# day1_part1 · shared setup. Economist editorial palette + IBM Plex Mono.
# Datasets come from the genomics_course package (no simulation in slides).
# (This block can later move into genomics_course.theme and be imported.)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib as mpl, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.font_manager as fm
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from pathlib import Path
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── course datasets (parquet loaders in the package) ────────────────────────
from genomics_course.data import (
    load_deseq2, load_admixture, load_gwas, load_variants,
    load_lineages, load_timecourse, load_coexpression,
    load_anscombe, load_datasaurus,
)

# ── register IBM Plex Mono from the repo's fonts/ folder ─────────────────────
_font_dir = None
for _cand in (Path("../fonts/IBM_Plex_Mono"), Path("fonts/IBM_Plex_Mono"),
              Path("../../fonts/IBM_Plex_Mono")):
    if _cand.exists():
        _font_dir = _cand
        break
if _font_dir is not None:
    for _ttf in _font_dir.glob("*.ttf"):
        fm.fontManager.addfont(str(_ttf))
    _MONO = "IBM Plex Mono"
else:
    _MONO = "DejaVu Sans Mono"

# ── Economist categorical palette (the "story" five) ────────────────────────
GREEN  = "#379A8B"   # green-teal, carries the story
BLUE   = "#006BA2"
AMBER  = "#EBB434"
RED    = "#B4405F"   # highlight
PURPLE = "#9A607F"   # highlight
GREY   = "#B3B3B3"

# ── neutrals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INK   = "#0D0D0D"
CREAM = "#FAF9F7"
LINE  = "#D9D9D9"
MUTED = "#666666"

# ── full Economist base ramps ───────────────────────────────────────────────
ECON = {
    "chicago":   ["#141F52", "#1F2E7A", "#2E45B8", "#475ED1", "#D6DBF5", "#EBEDFA"],
    "hongkong":  ["#169C7F", "#1DC9A4", "#36E2BD", "#D2F9F0", "#E9FCF8"],
    "newyork":   ["#F9C31F", "#FBD051", "#FCDE83", "#FEF2CD", "#FEF8E6"],
    "shanghai":  ["#4C9C16", "#62C91D", "#7BE236", "#E2F9D2", "#F0FCE9"],
    "singapore": ["#F97A1F", "#FB9851", "#FCB583", "#FEE1CD", "#FEF0E6"],
    "tokyo":     ["#9C1633", "#C91D42", "#E2365B", "#F9D2DB", "#FCE9ED"],
    "red":       ["#CC100A", "#E3120B", "#F6423C", "#FEE7E7"],
    "london":    ["#0D0D0D", "#1A1A1A", "#333333", "#595959", "#666666",
                  "#B3B3B3", "#D9D9D9", "#F2F2F2", "#FFFFFF"],
    "canvas":    ["#D0D3E1", "#E0E2EB", "#EFF0F5"],
}

COURSE_PAL = [GREEN, BLUE, AMBER, RED, PURPLE]
ECON_QUAL  = [ECON["chicago"][2], ECON["hongkong"][0], ECON["newyork"][0],
              ECON["shanghai"][1], ECON["tokyo"][1], ECON["singapore"][0]]

def econ_cmap(ramp="chicago", reverse=False):
    """Continuous colormap from one named Economist ramp."""
    cols = ECON[ramp][::-1] if reverse else ECON[ramp]
    return LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(f"econ_{ramp}", cols)

econ_diverging = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("econ_div", [BLUE, CREAM, RED])

# full-spectrum ramp for many-component stacks (blue→teal→green→amber→red)
econ_spectrum = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("econ_spectrum",
    [ECON["chicago"][2], ECON["hongkong"][0], ECON["shanghai"][1],
     ECON["newyork"][0], ECON["red"][1]])

# ── matplotlib defaults ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mpl.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": CREAM, "axes.facecolor": CREAM, "savefig.facecolor": CREAM,
    "font.family": _MONO,
    "axes.edgecolor": LINE, "axes.labelcolor": MUTED,
    "xtick.color": MUTED, "ytick.color": MUTED,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "font.size": 12,
})
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)

# ── pipeline flowchart helper (auto-shrinks long labels to fit) ─────────────
def pipeline_flowchart(steps, figsize=None):
    """Horizontal pipeline. Pass (label, desc) tuples or bare strings.
    Font auto-shrinks so labels never overflow their box."""
    norm = [(s if isinstance(s, str) else s[0]) for s in steps]
    n = len(norm)
    if figsize is None:
        figsize = (max(11, n * 2.0), 2.0)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize, facecolor=CREAM)
    ax.set_xlim(0, n); ax.set_ylim(0, 1); ax.axis("off")
    light = ECON["hongkong"][3]
    for i, label in enumerate(norm):
        last = (i == n - 1)
        bg, fg = (GREEN, "white") if last else (light, INK)
        ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch(
            (i + 0.06, 0.24), 0.88, 0.52,
            boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=0.08",
            facecolor=bg, edgecolor=GREEN, linewidth=1.4))
        fs = 10.5 if len(label) <= 16 else 9 if len(label) <= 24 else 7.5
        ax.text(i + 0.5, 0.5, label, ha="center", va="center",
                fontsize=fs, fontweight="bold", color=fg, wrap=True)
        if not last:
            ax.annotate("", xy=(i + 1.06, 0.5), xytext=(i + 0.94, 0.5),
                        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=LINE, lw=1.4, mutation_scale=16))
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig

<!-- slide 3 -->
## Anscombe's Quartet {.smaller}

[Why we visualise · summary stats lie]{.eyebrow}

### Four datasets, identical statistics, four different shapes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
```python
from genomics_course.data import load_anscombe
aq = load_anscombe()
aq.head(2)
# →   dataset     x     y
#   0       I  10.0  8.04
#   1       I   8.0  6.95

# 4 panels, one per dataset, shared scales
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8, 5.6),
                      sharex=True, sharey=True)
for a, (name, g) in zip(ax.flat,
                        aq.groupby("dataset")):
    a.scatter(g.x, g.y, color=GREEN, s=45)
    m, b = np.polyfit(g.x, g.y, 1)
    xs = np.linspace(g.x.min(), g.x.max(), 50)
    a.plot(xs, m*xs + b, color=RED, lw=1.6)
    a.set_title(f"dataset {name}")
```
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.6
aq = load_anscombe()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8, 5.6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, (name, g) in zip(axes.flat, aq.groupby("dataset")):
    ax.scatter(g.x, g.y, color=GREEN, s=55, edgecolors=CREAM, zorder=3)
    m, b = np.polyfit(g.x, g.y, 1)
    xs = np.linspace(g.x.min(), g.x.max(), 50)
    ax.plot(xs, m * xs + b, color=RED, lw=1.8, zorder=2)
    ax.set_title(f"dataset {name}", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
fig.suptitle("SAME STATS, DIFFERENT SHAPES", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Always plot your data. Summary statistics can hide everything that matters. *(Anscombe 1973)*
:::


<!-- slide 4 -->
## The Datasaurus Dozen {.smaller}

[Why we visualise · summary stats lie]{.eyebrow}

### Thirteen datasets, near-identical stats, wildly different shapes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
```python
from genomics_course.data import load_datasaurus
dd = load_datasaurus()
dd.head(2)
# →   dataset      x      y
#   0    dino  55.38  97.18
#   1    dino  51.54  96.03

# 3 x 5 grid of mini scatters
names = dd.dataset.unique()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(8.4, 5.4))
for a, name in zip(ax.flat, names):
    g = dd[dd.dataset == name]
    a.scatter(g.x, g.y, color=GREEN, s=5, alpha=0.7)
    a.set_title(name, fontsize=8)
    a.set_xticks([]); a.set_yticks([])
for a in ax.flat[len(names):]:
    a.axis("off")
```
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 8.4
#| fig-height: 5.4
dd = load_datasaurus()
names = dd["dataset"].unique()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(8.4, 5.4))
for ax, name in zip(axes.flat, names):
    g = dd[dd["dataset"] == name]
    ax.scatter(g.x, g.y, color=GREEN, s=6, alpha=0.75, edgecolors="none")
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_visible(False)
for ax in axes.flat[len(names):]:
    ax.axis("off")
fig.suptitle("ALL 13 SHARE THE SAME MEANS", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Numbers say the same thing; pictures say otherwise. *(Matejka & Fitzmaurice 2017)*
:::

<!-- slide 8 -->
## The Anatomy of a Matplotlib Figure {.smaller}

[Matplotlib · anatomy]{.eyebrow}

### Figure, Axes, and the artists drawn on top

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
A **Figure** is the whole canvas. Inside it sit one or more **Axes** (one plot,
with its own x and y). Everything you draw, lines, points, labels, ticks, is an
**artist** living on an Axes. Almost every plot starts with the same line that
*creates* the figure and axes:

```python
# CREATE the figure (canvas) and one axes (the plot)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))

# CALL a plotting method on that axes
ax.plot(x, y)
```

`fig` is the page; `ax` is the chart on it; everything else is an artist you add
to `ax`.
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.7
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
ax.plot(x, np.sin(x), color=GREEN, lw=2.5)
ax.set_xlabel("x axis label"); ax.set_ylabel("y axis label")
ax.set_title("FIGURE TITLE", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK, pad=10)
ann = dict(fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", color=RED,
           arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=RED, lw=1.3))
ax.annotate("Axes (one plot)", xy=(5, 0), xytext=(5.4, 0.7), **ann)
ax.annotate("artist (line)", xy=(1.6, 1.0), xytext=(2.2, 0.45), **ann)
ax.annotate("tick + label", xy=(0, -1.0), xytext=(1.0, -0.6), **ann)
fig.text(0.01, 0.97, "Figure (whole canvas)", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", color=BLUE)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.58em; color: #808080;"}
`fig` = canvas · `ax` = one plot · lines/points/labels = artists.
:::


<!-- slide 9.1 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 1: the canvas {.smaller}

[Matplotlib · build loop]{.eyebrow}

### Load real data, create the figure, label the frame

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
We build one figure across four slides, on one gene from the time-course data.
The data is six genes over five timepoints:

| gene | time | tpm | sem |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| BRCA1 | 0 | 13.0 | 3.06 |
| BRCA1 | 2 | 15.0 | 1.90 |
| BRCA1 | 6 | 17.0 | 2.32 |

```python
from genomics_course.data import load_timecourse
tc = load_timecourse()                     # gene, time, tpm, sem
g = tc[tc.gene == "BRCA1"]                  # keep one gene

# CREATE the canvas + axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)")                  # label the frame first
ax.set_ylabel("Expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(-1, 25)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.7
tc = load_timecourse(); g = tc[tc.gene == "BRCA1"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)"); ax.set_ylabel("Expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(-1, 25); ax.set_ylim(0, g.tpm.max() * 1.3)
ax.set_title("STEP 1: THE CANVAS", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=MUTED, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 9.2 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 2: add the data {.smaller}

[Matplotlib · build loop]{.eyebrow}

### Call a plotting method to draw the trajectory

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
The new line is the **call** that actually draws something: `ax.plot`. Markers
mark the measured timepoints; the line connects them.

```python
# ... step 1 (canvas) above ...

# CALL: draw the expression trajectory on the axes
ax.plot(g.time, g.tpm,                     # x, y
        marker="o",                        # show each timepoint
        color=GREEN,                       # story colour
        lw=2)                              # line width
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.7
tc = load_timecourse(); g = tc[tc.gene == "BRCA1"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)"); ax.set_ylabel("Expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(-1, 25); ax.set_ylim(0, g.tpm.max() * 1.3)
ax.plot(g.time, g.tpm, marker="o", color=GREEN, lw=2, markersize=7)
ax.set_title("STEP 2: ADD THE DATA", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=GREEN, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 9.3 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 3: show uncertainty {.smaller}

[Matplotlib · build loop]{.eyebrow}

### Shade the standard-error band behind the line

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
The dataset carries a `sem` column. A shaded band reads more quietly than error
bars and keeps the line clean. Note the bracket access `g["sem"]`, since `sem`
collides with a pandas method name.

```python
# ... steps 1-2 above ...

# CALL: fill a band of mean +/- standard error
ax.fill_between(g.time,                    # x
                g.tpm - g["sem"],          # lower edge
                g.tpm + g["sem"],          # upper edge
                color=GREEN, alpha=0.15)   # faint fill
# draw the line on top so it stays readable
ax.plot(g.time, g.tpm, marker="o", color=GREEN, lw=2)
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.7
tc = load_timecourse(); g = tc[tc.gene == "BRCA1"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)"); ax.set_ylabel("Expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(-1, 25); ax.set_ylim(0, g.tpm.max() * 1.3)
ax.fill_between(g.time, g.tpm - g["sem"], g.tpm + g["sem"], color=GREEN, alpha=0.15)
ax.plot(g.time, g.tpm, marker="o", color=GREEN, lw=2, markersize=7)
ax.set_title("STEP 3: SHOW UNCERTAINTY", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=INK, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 9.4 -->
## Building a Plot · Step 4: the message {.smaller}

[Matplotlib · build loop]{.eyebrow}

### A title that states the finding, not the variable name

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
The recipe, every time: **canvas, data, uncertainty, message.** The title says
what the chart *shows*, and one annotation points at it.

```python
# ... steps 1-3 above ...

# CALL: annotate the peak and title the finding
peak = g.loc[g.tpm.idxmax()]               # row with the max
ax.annotate("peak",
            xy=(peak.time, peak.tpm),      # point at it
            xytext=(peak.time + 3, peak.tpm),
            color=RED, fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=RED))
ax.set_title("BRCA1 RESPONDS WITHIN HOURS")
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.7
tc = load_timecourse(); g = tc[tc.gene == "BRCA1"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.7))
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)"); ax.set_ylabel("Expression (TPM)")
ax.set_xlim(-1, 25); ax.set_ylim(0, g.tpm.max() * 1.3)
ax.fill_between(g.time, g.tpm - g["sem"], g.tpm + g["sem"], color=GREEN, alpha=0.15)
ax.plot(g.time, g.tpm, marker="o", color=GREEN, lw=2, markersize=7)
peak = g.loc[g.tpm.idxmax()]
ax.annotate("peak", xy=(peak.time, peak.tpm), xytext=(peak.time + 3, peak.tpm),
            fontsize=9, color=RED, fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=RED))
ax.set_title("BRCA1 RESPONDS WITHIN HOURS", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold", color=GREEN, pad=10)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
Every plot in this course follows the same loop: canvas, data, uncertainty, message.
:::
